#### 1. pulmonary venoocclusive disease 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.477)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-201451)

**Proposed mechanism:** ACVRL1 (HGNC:73) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-912743); BMPR2 (HGNC:1100) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-912743); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-912743) —LEADS_TO→ Hemorrhagic telangiectasias (HP:0001604); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-912743) —LEADS_TO→ Pulmonary hypertension (HP:0002094); Pulmonary hypertension (HP:0002094) —LEADS_TO→ Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (HP:0001605). Mutations in ACVRL1 (HHT2) and BMPR2 (PVOD1) both converge on the disruption of the TGF-beta signaling pathway. Dysregulation of this pathway leads to distinct but related vascular pathologies: abnormal vessel formation manifesting as hemorrhagic telangiectasias in HHT2, and pulmonary vascular remodeling leading to pulmonary hypertension and veno-occlusive disease in PVOD1.

**How to falsify it:** If studies demonstrate that ACVRL1 and BMPR2 function in completely independent and non-interacting signaling branches downstream of TGF-beta, or if genetic variants in ACVRL1 are found to be benign in individuals with PVOD1, and vice versa, this proposed overlap would be falsified. _(variant: rs143704417)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TGF-beta signaling in these distinct vascular disorders could reveal common therapeutic targets. Modulating TGF-beta pathway activity might offer a unified approach to managing both hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and pulmonary venoocclusive disease, potentially improving treatments for patients with either condition.
